(a) BACKLOG TRUTH: the $14.1B is not stale, cherry-picked or segment-aggregated - the 24 July 2026 call states a record $14.1B, +$5.9B (73%) year on year with $5.6B of that same-store, and +$1.6B sequential of which $1.4B same-store, plus $510M of modular bookings above burn disclosed in the MD&A; implied book-to-bill near 1.5x on $3.27B of quarterly revenue holds. (b) GM-TRAJECTORY TRUTH: the claimed 23.5% - 24.8% - 25.5% - 26.3% - 25.9% series is not asserted from a proxy, it recomputes exactly off reported gross profit / revenue in the filed statements (Q2 2026: 845,013/3,265,656 = 25.88%; Q2 2025: 509,897/2,173,319 = 23.46%), and the ex-one-off 25.2% to 25.9% step is management's own quantified bridge. (c) THESIS WEAKNESS: demand is named and specific to FIX, not a theme borrowed from the grid/AI story - Electrical segment revenue +81% year on year ($968.99M vs $534.65M), modular capacity 3.5M sq ft going to ~5M by late summer 2027, and the 4-to-5M sq ft expansion answered flatly as being 'For current customers' with 'the 2 hyperscalers that we work with... willing to continue to provide us volume commitments' (24 July 2026). (d) HIDDEN DISQUALIFIER: none found that the record has not already priced - the two-hyperscaler concentration with no 10%-customer disclosure is stated in the record; there is no dilution risk (net cash $1,526.8M, funded borrowings $54.06M, $288.8M of H1 capex covered ~4.3x by $1,239M of H1 free cash flow) and no regulatory/queue gate on revenue. The only thing that broke was a supporting evidence number, not the valuation: the record's 'roughly $8.2M' of first-half 2026 repurchases is 3x too low ($24.997M actually spent), and the CFO's most recent dated statement on the stock cuts the other way from the record's February 2026 quote.
